objective: Give a self-contained finite-counting proof and deterministic finite selector for simple connected bipartite no-MC graphs of unbounded girth at fixed d0=41, without LPS or external existence theorems.

atomic_claims.text: For the union of 40 uniform permutation matchings on two N=M^2 parts, M>=1000, the probability of any smaller shore with crossing count <=2s is <1/20+1/1000.
With K=2g and C_g=K^2(160K^2)^K, the probability of two distinct cycles shorter than g sharing a vertex is <=C_g/N for N>=2K, including parallel pairs.
Taking M=max(1000,4C_g,2g) gives a finite bad-event bound <41/800<1, so a tuple with both cut expansion and disjoint short cycles exists.
One edge deleted per vertex-disjoint short cycle is a matching deletion; the resulting graph is simple, bipartite, degrees 39 or 40, girth>=g and every cut exceeds its smaller shore.
The lexicographically first good tuple and canonical cycle-edge deletion define a deterministic finite family with average<=40<41 and girth>=g for every g>=3.

assumptions: Final witnesses obey the frozen finite-simple-graph and nonempty-shore semantics.
Auxiliary coloured multigraphs and their length-two cycles are explicitly distinguished from final simple witnesses.
Probabilities are exact ratios in a finite uniform space of 40-tuples of permutations; no random-graph existence theorem is used.
Only finite counting, elementary graph arguments and rational inequalities are mathematical premises.
risks: No sampler, graph generator, SAT solver, spectral code, proof assistant or mathematical verifier was run.
The all-shore union bound, same-colour permutation constraints and overlapping-cycle pattern count require trusted audit.
The deterministic selector is extremely inefficient and has not been executed; the JSON is a parametric specification, not a receipt.
Both admitted obligations remain open until the required trusted verification and admission chain is completed.
